articles.title: Madueke scores only goal as below-par Arsenal beat Nottingham Forest
articles.summary: Arsenal did not register a shot on target until Noni Madueke bagged their winner 10 minutes from full-time.
articles.body:
Noni Madueke’s late goal sealed Arsenal’s 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest as the champions survived a scrappy display to close the gap on Premier League leaders Manchester City.

Mikel Arteta’s side were well below their best at the City Ground on Sunday and did not register a shot on target until Madueke bagged their winner 10 minutes from full-time.

While the Gunners earned few style points in the East Midlands, they will not be overly concerned after moving to within three points of table-toppers City, who beat Ipswich 3-2 on Saturday.

After a shock 3-0 loss at Brighton on September 19 , second-placed Arsenal have bounced back with three successive victories.

They beat Leeds in the Premier League and Lille in the Champions League, before their hard-fought success by the banks of the River Trent.

The north Londoners have not been able to recapture the relentless consistency that took them to their first title in 22 years last season.

But they retain the priceless ability to grind out wins and this was their sixth in seven league matches.

Arsenal head to Bayern Munich in the Champions League on Wednesday before hosting Everton in the top flight next weekend.

Third-from-bottom Forest have won just twice at home in their last 17 league games, while boss Oliver Glasner has managed only one victory in seven top-flight matches since taking charge in the close season.

Bukayo Saka’s cross forced Forest goalkeeper Matz Sels to claw the ball from under his crossbar, but Arsenal struggled to establish any rhythm in a scrappy opening.

Forest’s Dan Ndoye tested Arsenal keeper David Raya after drifting in at the far post.

In a rare threat from Arteta’s men, Kai Havertz fired into the side-netting from an acute angle after Martin Odegaard’s pass opened up the Forest defence.

Arteta looked increasingly frustrated on the touchline as a turgid half petered out.

Eberechi Eze paid the price for Arsenal’s lethargy as the England forward was replaced by Madueke at the interval.

There was no immediate improvement from Arsenal despite that change and Forest striker Liam Delap drilled just wide after a rampaging run.

Arsenal were too slow in possession and lacked penetration when they went forward, so Arteta introduced Mikel Merino, Viktor Gyokeres and Jurrien Timber in a bid to ignite a revival.

Bruno Guimaraes was one of the Arsenal players sacrificed after another underwhelming display from the Brazil midfielder in only his second league start since his summer move from Newcastle.

Gabriel Magalhaes headed over from a Declan Rice corner, while Delap could not muster the accuracy to beat Raya from Xaver Schlager’s pass.

Odegaard picked out Timber’s run and the defender teed up Declan Rice inside the Forest area, but his wasteful shot ballooned over, encapsulating the visitors’ impotence.

It was the first time since 2023 that Arsenal had failed to have a shot on target in the first 70 minutes of a Premier League match.

But they finally made the breakthrough in the 80th minute as Madueke cut in from the left flank and unleashed a powerful drive that took a hefty deflection off Forest’s Jair Cunha as it flashed past Sels.

Murillo was inches away from snatching a late leveller for Forest as the defender’s rocket whistled over.

articles.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick must not be in bottom half come January, warns Gary Neville after Leeds draw
articles.summary: Man Utd's winless run stretched to six games as Dominic Calvert-Lewin's second-half strike from a corner cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's opener to leave Michael Carrick's side in 13th after claiming just one win in their first seven Premier League matches this season
articles.body:
United have just seven points from seven league matches, winning just one of those, which is their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight season for 40 years.

Despite extending their winless run in all competitions to six games with the draw at Elland Road, the performance was much improved, with Carrick's tactical tweaks making his side more compact and defensively solid.

Neville agreed with the United head coach's assessment that Sunday's performance at Elland Road was a step in the right direction.

Speaking on the Gary Neville podcast , the Sky Sports pundit said: "[There's] a depressed standard and a low expectation right now.

"But it'll feel like a stepping stone for Michael Carrick, and it'll feel like the first step on the ladder in the Premier League.

"They may take some confidence from that, and there might be a blueprint there. Maybe we have to bring Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford and others off the bench, and we might just have to have a go at being more solid."

'Carrick's got a problem if Man Utd 13th in January'

United's paltry points return has them sitting 13th in the Premier League after seven games, already five points adrift of fifth place, which was enough for Champions League qualification last season.

Neville says there is no need for panic just yet but feels United have to show signs of improvement over the next few weeks otherwise Carrick could find himself in hot water come the new year.

"I would say fourth would be a birdie, fifth would be par, and sixth would be a bogey," said Neville of his former club's targets for the season. "But they can't finish outside the top five, because then you're missing out on Champions League and it becomes a vicious circle.

"Then you can't get those players because they want to play in the Champions League and you can't get the money from it and you've lost the £60m-£70m and you're in the Europa League on Thursday nights.

"Fifth is a must for Michael Carrick to continue to grow and Manchester United continue to grow with investment.

"If they're 13th in January, he's got a problem because then you are what you are. Whereas I think it's still early enough, seven points from seven games, to say, 'okay, still early in the season'. You can't say that after 15 games.

"It has to change in the next few weeks: Bournemouth is really important and Chelsea away. And how he manages the games in between that.

"You've got to say fifth. You know that anything less than fifth is going to be a disappointment and a dropping standard from the start of the season where everybody expected them to finish.

"And at the moment, they're well short of that because you look at Brighton, Liverpool, Aston Villa - they look like they're picking up a little bit. It's difficult."

'Baleba staying fit is going to be critical'

Neville has seen encouraging signs from Carlos Baleba's start to life as a Manchester United player and feels the midfielder staying fit is crucial for Carrick this season.

Signed from Brighton for £70m at the end of the summer window, the 21-year-old arrived with an ankle injury that has kept him from featuring until he came on in the second half of last Saturday's 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham.

Baleba has started the last two games, at Atletico Madrid and Leeds, and brought an added steel to United's midfield alongside fellow summer-signing Andrey Santos.

"I know he had a difficult season last year at Brighton, but you watch him in his first couple of games or so for United, and he's got something," said Neville. "He's got a bit of strength about him, he's got a presence.

"Him staying fit is gonna be absolutely critical, I can understand why Michael Carrick took him off with 20 minutes to go [at Leeds], because he's played [nearly] three games in a week.

"Maybe he doesn't play him against Como on Wednesday. We're not throwing the Champions League away, but Manchester United have to beat Bournemouth next weekend.

"I just wonder whether that Santos-Baleba partnership is going to stay there for a bit, and let a couple of [the attacking players] float around in front, and be a lot more solid, make sure we're not giving as much space away.

"I'm sick of Manchester United's team being easy to play against, and Michael Carrick will be sick of it."

articles.title: Celtic 7-1 Hearts: Kris Boyd praises 'devastating' Hoops as Hearts' tactics questioned
articles.summary: Celtic beat Hearts 7-1 to move four points clear at the top of the Scottish Premiership; Hearts have not won outside Edinburgh since January; Martin O'Neill's side are away to Hibernian in their next league game on October 25, live on Sky Sports; Hearts face Motherwell on same day
articles.body:
After last season's final-day showdown, the Hoops reminded Wouter Vrancken's team what it takes to win the league trophy with a "devastating" performance.

It is a result that moves Martin O'Neill's men four points clear at the top of the table with Hearts left in third, a further four points behind Rangers.

Encouraged by their second-half showing in Thursday's 3-1 Europa League defeat to Benfica, the manager started with the front three that finished that game in Lisbon.

And all three - Benjamin Nygren, Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran - scored in the 7-1 demolition of their title rivals.

Celtic were outstanding at times but Hearts played a part in their own humiliation.

"That first half was devastating. Hearts, I cannot for the life of me work out what they were trying to do there," said Kris Boyd.

"To come here and show the lack of respect to Celtic that Hearts have done today would be a wake-up call for me.

"You look at last year, Derek McInnes [then Hearts boss] got criticised for it from a lot of people in terms of just grinding out results. It may be an ugly watch but they were still there.

"I don't see any of that Hearts team that's going in the Celtic team. I don't see any of it, so what would make you think you're better than them?"

"That there was an annihilation. I mean, I have never seen anything like it in my life."

Hearts had only conceded eight goals in the Premiership this season, before shipping seven in 90 minutes at Celtic Park.

"I couldn't work out if Hearts were really poor or Celtic were really good. It's probably a combination of the two of them," said former Hearts defender Ryan McGowan.

"The amount of times that Hearts gave the ball away in really dangerous areas for Celtic, and there would only be two passes and it was a goal, and they continually did it throughout the whole game.

"There is levels to football. Hearts obviously last season went close and this season they want to challenge it and be up there. But you also have to understand the game.

"They're 5-1 down at half-time and then whatever the manager said to them went completely out of their ears because then they conceded another goal four minutes into the second half.

"It was a really poor performance from Hearts, which you haven't said that often in the last 12 months. At the same time, you've got to give Celtic a lot of credit."

It was all too easy for Celtic on Sunday but that did not mean Martin O'Neill was ruling Hearts out of this season's title race after just nine games.

"It's easy to be magnanimous after the game but they're still big challengers," the 74-year-old told Sky Sports .

"Everything clicked for us today. We might have had two more chances but everything that we hit went into the net.

"It was nice to win today because I was concerned after Thursday night, wondering how we feel, can we get ourselves together for it?

"You ask any manager or any team, any player, they would say the same thing. Once you've put a couple of goals in front, then confidence just is so strong.

"The team played with a lot of confidence but you have to gain that confidence in the first place. And that's what we did today."

While Celtic welcome Benfica in the Europa League on Thursday night, Hearts are away to Trabzonspor in the Conference League.

"When you're not on top level in the top games, then it's really difficult to get a result," Hearts head coach Wouter Vrancken told Sky Sports .

"It's good to analyse it, also the good things. Knowing where we come from and not losing the grip and confidence in what you're doing. We just have to do things better than today.

"It was not good enough because of the individual mistakes and the two set plays which killed us at the beginning of the game.

"We made mistakes that we wouldn't normally make. That's it. I'm sorry."

Suffice it to say, the Associated Press Top 25 poll looks a lot different after a consequential Saturday in college football.

BYU, Ohio State, Notre Dame and Georgia fill out the top five.

Big 12 Admits Error on Clock Controversy

Multiple controversial finishes and more takeaways from CFB Week 7

Alabama and Texas slipped to 13th and 19th, respectively, after suffering their second defeats on the season.

Georgia had a golden opportunity to pull through with a win at home. With a little over a minute remaining, the Bulldogs started from their own 39-yard line and then crossed into Auburn territory thanks to a pass interference penalty.

Then quarterback Gunner Stockton coughed it up for his third turnover of the day and Auburn recovered. Eventually, the Tigers' Alex McPherson drilled a 34-yard field goal as time expired.

For Notre Dame and Indiana, the margins in their defeats couldn't have been much slimmer.

The Big 12 acknowledged one more second should've been added to the clock in the Fighting Irish's 28-24 loss to BYU. At the very least, they would've had another opportunity to score from the 8-yard line, and a pass interference penalty, which also was missed, would've moved them closer to the goal line for one final play.

Over in Bloomington, Hoosiers wide receiver Nick Marsh was inches away from hauling in a go-ahead touchdown reception with just over a minute left. The junior seemed to recognize immediately his left foot landed out of bounds, resigning the reigning national champions to a 19-15 loss.

Neither Alabama nor Texas can feel too hard done by given the nature of their upsets.

Crimson Tide quarterback Keelon Russell saw his Heisman Trophy campaign hit a snag as he went 19-of-29 for 147 yards and two interceptions. The Tide defense, meanwhile, allowed Tennessee running back DeSean Bishop to go for 159 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.

The Longhorns couldn't maintain the 17-3 lead they built midway through the second quarter. It was yet another lackluster showing from their offense, which left coach Steve Sarkisian pledging to evaluate everything including a possible quarterback change.

BYU's win wasn't the only notable result involving the Big 12.

Houston earned a signature win over Oklahoma State, 35-32, to improve to 6-1 on the year. Cougars quarterback Conner Weigman out-dueled the Cowboys' Drew Mestemaker. The pair of signal-callers combined to throw for 708 yards and eight touchdowns.

Mestemaker got the deficit down to three points in the fourth quarter with a 66-yard touchdown pass to Caleb Hawkins. Weigman responded with a 48-yard touchdown throw to Koby Young to make it a two-score game again with 9:48 remaining.

Houston moved up from 20th to 14th with the victory.

The Cougars are in the think of a tight Big 12 title race that involves BYU, Texas Tech and Utah, all of whom are unbeaten overall.

articles.summary: The most significant changes in the AP Top 25 this season occurred in Sunday's poll.
articles.body:
The most significant changes in the AP Top 25 this season occurred in Sunday's poll.

The Miami Hurricanes are the new No. 1 team after the losses suffered by the Georgia Bulldogs and Notre Dame Fighting Irish.

The BYU Cougars, who beat Notre Dame at home on Saturday night, vaulted all the way up to No. 2 in Sunday's poll.

BYU is now one of three Big 12 teams inside the top 10, along with the Texas Tech Red Raiders at No. 8 and the Utah Utes at No. 10.

Notre Dame only fell two spots to No. 4, which is one spot ahead of UGA, who was the top team last week.

UGA is one of two SEC teams inside the top 10, and while that may seem like a marginal total, the first three spots outside the top 10 are occupied by SEC programs.

Miami assumed the No. 1 spot in the AP Top 25 after the losses suffered by Georgia and Notre Dame.

The Hurricanes had to fight hard to get out of Week 7 with an undefeated record, as the Florida State Seminoles pushed them to double overtime on Saturday night.

Miami is now 6-0 with one big game left on its schedule, a road trip to Notre Dame Stadium on November 7.

That contest will likely be a battle of top-five teams, and in Miami's case, a test of whether it can compete with one of the top programs in the sport.

In fact, the trip to South Bend is only one of two true road games left on Miami's regular-season schedule. The other is a visit to face the North Carolina Tar Heels on October 31.

At minimum, Miami should finish the regular season at 11-1. A win over Notre Dame likely means the Hurricanes go 12-0 and land the top spot in the CFB Playoff rankings.

BYU's home win over Notre Dame and the handful of losses within the top eight allowed the Cougars to vault up to No. 2.

BYU is now in fantastic shape to qualify for the CFB playoff, whether it be as the Big 12 champion, or as an at-large team.

The Cougars have one of the best wins of any team in the country and they should go 11-1 or 12-0.

BYU's biggest test will be a road trip across the state to play the Utah Utes on November 7.

Utah is a top-10 team now as well. That gives BYU the opportunity to have a pair of top-10 victories on its resume, something other contenders for a first-round bye will not have in their possession.

BYU's win was also massive for the Big 12 as a whole. Texas Tech and Utah are both inside the top 10, but they are at the back end of the top 10. BYU now has cushion to get in as an at-large if it loses to Utah, or in the Big 12 Championship Game.

Texas Tech has one Top 25 foe on its schedule, while Utah has two. There's a real chance all three of the Big 12's best teams make the playoff now given the lack of quality in the ACC as well as the parity in the SEC and Big Ten.

SEC Contenders Still Trying To Sort Themselves Out

The SEC only has Georgia and Ole Miss inside the top 10 going into Week 8.

Tennessee, Kentucky and Alabama sit at Nos. 11, 12 and 13, while Texas is down to No. 19 and Florida sits at No. 20.

Georgia, Kentucky, Tennessee and Ole Miss are tied at the top of the conference with one league loss each. Alabama and Texas already have two SEC defeats.

UGA and Ole Miss are the top-ranked teams for now, but the Rebels have to go to Austin next week to play Texas. Georgia still has to play Florida and Ole Miss.

The high amount of parity across the conference makes it difficult to decipher which teams will make the 12-team field.

That's a big benefit for teams from the other power conferences, but it also opens up the possibility for a three-loss SEC team to enter the playoff if the top programs continue to beat each other.

articles.title: Hearts roll out red carpet... and Celtic walk all over it
articles.summary: Hearts thought attack was the best form of defence at Celtic Park. They were badly wrong, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
Jimmy Thunder was having none of Crawford Grimsley's chutzpah, none of his mouthing off before their heavyweight contest back in the late 1990s, none of his pre-bout arrogance.

Thunder took precisely 1.5 seconds to put Grimsley down - one punch, an overhand right to his opponent's temple. Lights out. Fight over. Statement sent.

As Celtic unloaded on Hearts at Celtic Park it was football's equivalent of Thunder's devastation; speed and accuracy and ruthlessness in the face of a challenger akin to a rabbit caught in the headlights.

Hearts didn't give it the big one in the preamble to this evisceration, but they set up in the manner of a team who truly believed they were a whole lot better than they actually are.

Poor concentration and lack of physicality cost them two set-piece goals inside 10 minutes. The game was effectively over, but the visitors' suffering had only just begun.

Celtic score seven in humiliation of title rivals Hearts

All the latest Celtic news, views and analysis

Everything you need to know about Hearts

The pretenders came to Glasgow with a weak away record in the league - two wins in 11 between this season and the end of last, both against Hibs - and tried to go toe-to-toe.

Thinking attack is the best form of defence is all very well as long as you can back it up, as long as you can defend competently, as long as you can pass from A to B without losing your mind, as long as you don't concede acreage of space to exploit.

Time and again, Hearts rolled out the red carpet to Celtic.

A clinical Celtic made them pay for their naivety and maybe their arrogance, too. The footballing version of poor Crawford Grimsley. On their backside before they knew it.

Hearts played the highest line with slow defenders, they pushed up the park and left themselves exposed to Celtic's speedsters. That gameplan was not high-risk, it was reckless.

Martin O'Neill needed a win after his recent travails and this was a stroll in the park that he could not have imagined.

Football management can be a horribly stressful business that can put years on you. After this, O'Neill looked younger not older. The ageing process worked in reverse thanks to his team feasting on Hearts' scarcely believable weaknesses.

The stats are, frankly, hilarious. If it was a horrific day for Wouter Vrancken and his players then it was every bit as grim an experience for those who try to see sense in numbers.

Hearts had more shots than Celtic (20-18). They had more shots inside the box (16-13). They had more possession (52%-48%). They had more crosses (16-10). They won more duels (51%-49%). They had more passes in their opponents' half (244-202). They had more accurate passes (458-423).

That last one was laugh-out-loud funny, for Hearts' use of the ball was comically bad.

So often, when under a little bit of pressure, or no pressure at all, they passed into space only for Celtic to gobble up the loose ball and launch an attack which usually ended in a big chance or a goal.

The home team was slick. Benjamin Nygren, Callum Osmand, Camilo Duran and Haissem Hassan were devastating. Seven did not flatter them in the slightest.

It began with those two early goals - Liam Scales showing the desire to win a near-post header from a corner and Kieran Tierney left alone a few yards out to force in, then Dane Murray outfighting Claudio Braga to help it back to Nygren to score.

Hassan hit a post when he turned and darted away from Stephen Kingsley. People wondered what was Vrancken going to do to change this. Answer: nothing.

When Celtic score seven it seems odd to talk about pieces of defending they did that were significant, but Colby Donovan's cameos warrant mention.

Around the midpoint of the first half, Hearts stirred a little. You wouldn't say that they had momentum, but they had a bit of a possession and their hair-on-fire panic of the early minutes seemed under control.

Twice in the space of three minutes, Josh McPake - one of the form players in the country - took on Donovan and twice Donovan routed him.

Those little duels might disappear from relevance after the deluge, but at the time they were important. The Hearts dangerman had been snuffed out. His morale had taken a hiding. And the stadium loved it.

Hearts fell apart at the seams from there. Sabri Guendouz gave the ball away and Duran combined with the impressive Osmand to score number three.

Jamie McCart then became detached from his trolley and Celtic scored from that error, too. Osmand, again, but with lovely work from Duran. And easy, oh so easy.

Celtic's pace in attack was terrific. Their alertness was outstanding. Their disbelief was there, too. How could a team with a seemingly good coach and a strong squad of players be performing like a pub team?

Hearts fans started heading home at that point. They missed the goal that made it 4-1. They won't have shed any tears. Had they gone back they'd only have suffered on. Best get out of dodge as quickly as possible.

Soon, it was 5-1, Mika Baur slaloming his way past the comatose figures of McPake and Malachi Fagan-Walcott to dink a shot on goal, helped on its way by Kingsley and McCart, sitting on the floor, all flailing legs, like an octopus who had fallen out of a tree.

Can title race still be three-way fight?

Hearts' heads had long since gone. They were a broken team, psychologically. The doubt and fear coursed through their veins.

The easiest things became difficult. The difficult things became impossible. They had no discipline, no direction.

Vrancken spoke later about individual errors and that was obvious, but what else? He was given an opportunity to take some responsibility for the way he set his team up to begin with, but he declined to go there.

On reflection, maybe he will. He should. Gung-ho football is fine when it works. Unless it's laced with some pragmatism when facing the best teams in their own backyard then it can blow up in your face, which it did at Celtic Park.

Then it was 6-1 (Laurent Mendy the culprit, followed by McCart) and 7-1 (Tomas Magnusson in the frame). Duran and Nygren finished with aplomb. Seven minutes remained. The expectation was that this could still become eight or nine.

We like to think this league title race can be a three-horse thing again this season. We want the drama of last time.

Hearts played Celtic four times last term. They won two, drew one and lost one. They had nous and resilience before it all slowly slipped away from them.

This team has talent but, with their away record as it is, they're not going the distance, or anything close to the distance.

Celtic will be buoyed by this. Using it as fuel is the next step.

Osmand was a big player for them. O'Neill might have hit on a powerful front three that doesn't involve Kasper Hogh from the start.

After some rough days and nights they have some of their feelgood back. Keeping it on the long road ahead is the challenge now.

articles.title: AP Top 25: Miami, BYU take top 2 spots after a host of top-10 losses in Week 7
articles.summary: The Hurricanes beat Florida State in double overtime at home on Saturday.
articles.body:
The AP Top 25 looks a lot different after five of the top seven teams lost in Week 7.

A day after escaping in double overtime against Florida State at home, Miami basically became the No. 1 team in the country by default. The Hurricanes moved up to No. 1 after No. 1 Georgia lost at home to Auburn and No. 2 Notre Dame lost to BYU.

The Cougars moved up six spots to No. 2 after the controversial win over the Fighting Irish . BYU jumped ahead of Ohio State, who moved up a spot after beating Indiana on the road. Ohio State likely didn't move to No. 2 because of QB Julian Sayin's right shoulder injury . Buckeyes coach Ryan Day said Sayin is likely out "several weeks" after he was injured in the fourth quarter.

The top five is filled out by the Irish and Bulldogs. Indiana fell one spot to No. 6 and is followed by Ole Miss, Texas Tech, UCLA and Utah in the top 10. It's the first time Miami has been ranked No. 1 since the 2002 season, and BYU hasn't been in the top two of the AP Top 25 since 1984.

Texas dropped from No. 7 to No. 19 after it lost at home to unranked Florida. The Gators are now at No. 20. Texas became the first No. 1 team to lose back-to-back games to unranked teams with the loss to the Gators. The Longhorns lost the No. 1 ranking after a Week 6 loss to Oklahoma.

Alabama dropped from No. 6 to No. 13 after it lost to Tennessee. The Volunteers moved up to No. 11 with the home win. Since so many teams at the top of the poll lost, eight of the top 10 teams entering Week 7 stayed in the top 10.

There are also just six undefeated teams remaining in Miami, BYU, Texas Tech, UCLA, Utah and James Madison. The first five are in the top 10. The Dukes are unranked.

Week 8 could end up being a bit calmer than Week 7, though you should always be prepared for the unpredictable in college football. There are just two matchups between ranked teams, as Ole Miss heads to Texas and No. 14 Houston visits Utah. The Cougars moved up six spots with a win over Oklahoma State.

Three top-five teams — Ohio State, Notre Dame and Georgia — are all off in Week 8.

articles.body: Diego López, ex guardameta del Real Madrid y actual entrenador de porteros del filial, se estrenó en el Santiago Bernabéu llevando el calentamiento de Thibaut Courtois en la previa del Real Madrid - Sevilla. La sanción de Nuno Santos de un partido, por su expulsión ante el Villarreal, le ha abierto las puertas del primer equipo al menos para una noche. Diego López llegó al Real Madrid como entrenador de porteros de la mano de Álvaro Arbeloa, que lo quiso tener cerca cuando el técnico dio el salto al Real Madrid Castilla. Siguió en el filial cuando Arbeloa cogió las riendas del primer equipo y continuó con su trabajo en el Castilla con Julián López de Lerma. Diego López siempre fue un portero de la confianza de Mourinho. De hecho, fue él quién le fichó para el equipo blanco cuando Casillas se lesionó en la temporada 12-13 y el que le mantuvo en la titularidad cuando Iker se recuperó. Siempre han mantenido una estrecha relación y ahora vuelven a trabajar mano a mano, aunque sea por un partido por la sanción de Nuno, que estará en el Camp Nou el próximo domingo.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest 0-1 Arsenal: Noni Madueke's late deflected strike wins it with Gunners' only shot on target
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Noni Madueke’s deflected winner earned Arsenal a hard-fought victory at Nottingham Forest; the Gunners stay within three points of Premier League leaders Manchester City, while Forest drop into the relegation zone
articles.body:
After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.

However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

The result takes Arsenal to 18 points, three behind leaders Manchester City. For Forest, the frustration deepens. They drop into the relegation zone and are still waiting for their first home league goal of the season.

Analysis: Eze must prove his worth as Arsenal's main man after Madueke shines

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.

His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.

Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.

"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.

Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.

There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.

Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.

The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men."

Forest's lack of goals has caught up with them

There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.

Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.

Forest competed and created opportunities, but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.

Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility, but their attacking play lacked conviction.

That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving."

"That's the difference, you have to be clinical."

Glasner: Have to take your chances against the champions

"I think everybody feels the result is unfair today (in terms of the way we performed).

"But it's another defeat and another game when we couldn't score at the City Ground.

"But the performance today, especially defensively was of the top level.

"It was their only shot on target (that Arsenal scored from) and this one was deflected and Arsenal took the win.

"We also had our moments and it's important when you play the champions you take your moments.

articles.title: Free-scoring Brighton continue to impress and entertain as they thrash Palace
articles.summary: With 23 goals in seven Premier League matches, including some stunning strikes, Brighton continue to delight their fans and get them dreaming of what might be.
articles.body:
Not only are Brighton scoring more than everyone else in the Premier League, they are netting better goals too.

Centre-half Lewis Dunk won the Premier League goal of the month for September with a 35-yard stunner against Coventry . Now, five weeks later, that has already been eclipsed.

Step forward Seagulls team-mate Diego Gomez, who shot from the halfway line having seen Crystal Palace goalkeeper Walter Benitez off his line during Brighton's emphatic 5-0 win over their rivals on Sunday.

Benitez made a rapid dash back to his goal and produced a desperate dive but could not stop the ball going in just under the crossbar.

"As soon as he struck it, I knew it was in. He's taken the club goal of the season off me," joked Brighton skipper Dunk.

"That's the goal of the season so far, what a hit," added former Premier League striker Efan Ekoku, part of the commentary team for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra. "[It was] superbly struck and right over the head of the keeper from the centre-circle."

Gomez's seventh-minute goal at the Amex put Brighton 2-0 up and was from 51 metres, the furthest long-range Premier League goal since Wayne Rooney scored from 58m for Everton in their 4-0 win over West Ham in November 2017.

"When I scored, I didn't know where to run, or what to do," admitted 23-year-old Paraguay midfielder Gomez. "When I got the ball, I knew the goalkeeper was a little bit ahead. I was very happy with the goal."

Former Newcastle goalkeeper and Match of the Day pundit Shay Given said the goal was "reminiscent of David Beckham [for Manchester United versus Wimbledon in 1996]" and added: "I don't even blame Benitez the goalkeeper.

"We're always talking about sweeper goalkeepers and you've got to be high up for the through ball and the defence playing a high line. I think his position was fine.

"You've just got to take your hat off to Gomez. That is just a brilliant, brilliant goal."

Goalscoring Brighton only bettered by Barca

Brighton have never finished higher than sixth in English football's top flight, but now have 16 points from seven matches, with fan hopes rising that they could make a real push for Champions League qualification, or even a title challenge.

Their tally of 23 top-flight goals is four more than league leaders Manchester City , and more than double the 11 of reigning champions Arsenal .

Since the top flight was rebranded as the Premier League in 1992, only three sides have scored more goals across their first seven games of a season - Arsenal in 2009-10 (24), Manchester United in 2011-12 (24), and Manchester City in 2019-20 (27).

In the top five European leagues, only Barcelona, with 39 goals from nine La Liga matches, have more domestic league goals than Brighton .

With 10 different goalscorers, Brighton , third in the table, have also been the great entertainers of the season so far.

They won their opening league game 4-0 against an Aston Villa side that came fourth in 2025-26 and Fabian Hurzeler's team have shown that was not a one-off. Results since have included winning 5-0 at Coventry , 3-0 against Arsenal , 2-0 at Sunderland despite having a man sent off, and now 5-0 against rivals Palace.

In the Carabao Cup, they fought back from 2-0 down to win 3-2 at Old Trafford and eliminate Manchester United . In Europe, they have justified their position as Conference League favourites, putting four past both Norwegian side Tromso and Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris.

For Hurzeler, the youngest permanent manager in Premier League history when he was appointed in June 2024 at the age of 31, the atmosphere at the Amex could not have been any more different to their previous match with Palace.

When the Eagles won 1-0 in February, Brighton were 14th, had only won one of 12 league games with the home fans chanting "you're getting sacked in the morning" at their own boss.

Therefore, it is no surprise that Hurzeler is not getting carried away at his side's good form.

He was quick to shut down any talk that Brighton could be involved in the Premier League title race and said: "We have to stay very humble. The season will be long.

"We have to keep going. We can't be satisfied. We have to keep pushing, stay humble and understand why we are successful at the moment to keep pushing at that level."

The rapid rise of a former art dealer to Europe's hottest young manager

Hurzeler was also keen to ensure Gomez remained grounded.

"It's not simple to score a goal like this," added Hurzeler. "Everyone speaks about his goal, but to me the most important thing is the things we can improve, small easy passes we missed.

"It's good to celebrate the win but understand there is still space for improvement especially for individual players.

"We don't train shots from 50 metres. Overall, we know he has a really good finish. In these moments it's about being very precise with his long kick. The perception to recognise the keeper and be quick to go to the action was impressive."

Brighton fans will have to savour the memories of this win and Gomez's goal as all of their next five matches are away from home.

That run includes league games at Liverpool and Manchester City , another trip to Etihad Stadium in the last 16 of the Carabao Cup, as well as Conference League matches in Czech Republic and Spain, against Jablonec and Getafe respectively.

By the time Brighton return to the Amex on 8 November to face Brentford , we will have a better indication of just how optimistic the Seagulls fans can be about their season.

"I know it's rare, but you look at Leicester in 2016 and Blackburn in 1995 when I was a kid," added Given. "At the minute, you'd say they could upset the apple cart, but obviously it's a long winter coming up.

"Being in European competition as well, that will take its toll for sure. But they're having an unbelievable start to the season. Even set-plays as well, they're the best in the league (nine goals scored).

"They've scored the most goals overall and kept the joint-most goals out, so that's a good start for any team to do well, isn't it?!"
